notes: Double-barrelled: whether to fold the MBM deliverable market boundaries into the LBM hierarchy at all, and if so whether in addition to or as a replacement for the proposed spatial boundaries. notes: Comments on question 33, cited explicitly in the wording.

notes: Boilerplate; comments on the picklist in question 45, resolved via parent_question 45.

notes: Boilerplate; subject resolved via anchor_question 44. Answered by 455 against 390 for the support picklist.

notes: Boilerplate; comments on the picklist in question 47, resolved via parent_question 47.

label: Alignment with regional reporting programmes
notes: Asks for a named mandatory or voluntary programme and the effect of the revisions on alignment with it, so this is an evidence request rather than a stance. Invites concerns and support in the same box ("For concerns or support for alignment..."), so answers from both sides land in one field with nothing structured to separate them.

label: Requirement strength for local boundary
notes: Double-barrelled: why local boundary is too granular to require, and separately whether reporting at that granularity should be a "may", "should" or "shall not" requirement. The three-way normative choice is free text rather than a picklist, so it has to be hand-coded before it can be counted. Framed only from the concerned side, leaving respondents who think it should be required no natural place to say so.

label: When to require a non-accessible factor
notes: Triple-barrelled: the conditions under which a more accurate non-accessible factor should be required over an accessible one, the transparency and assurance that would have to accompany it, and any cost/effort implications. Three distinct asks in one free-text box, so few answers cover all three.

label: Decision-usefulness gain from LBM revisions
notes: NOT a support scale. An improvement ladder scored 0-3, from "No meaningful improvement" to "Substantial improvement", with "Not sure / no basis to assess" off-scale and null (72 respondents). The judgement is explicitly net of cost — "relative to incremental cost and complexity for preparers" — so a low score can mean either no benefit or a benefit outweighed by cost. Modal answer is "No meaningful improvement", 209 of 482.

label: Comments on LBM decision-usefulness
notes: Context for question 52, cited explicitly in the wording.

label: Comparability gain from LBM revisions
notes: NOT a support scale. The same 0-3 improvement ladder as question 52, worded for comparability rather than decision-usefulness. The trade-off clause differs from question 52 however: cost and complexity "for users" here against "for preparers" there. The same asymmetry recurs in the MBM pair (questions 134 and 136), so it is either deliberate or a drafting slip that propagated; either way the two ladders net out against different things and are not strictly comparable.

label: Comments on LBM comparability
notes: Context for question 54, cited explicitly in the wording.

label: Basis for LBM usefulness assessment
notes: Covers questions 52-55 jointly, so it cannot be attributed to the decision-usefulness or the comparability answer alone. Runs from "General awareness (no direct analysis)" (137) up to "Direct empirical analysis" (16): only 16 of 408 claim empirical backing, which bounds how much weight the question 52 and 54 ladders can carry.
